articles.title: El Manchester United se "hunde" en plena guerra civil: "Es una pu** vergüenza"
articles.standfirst: Las declaraciones de Lisandro Martínez contra la directiva han desatado una auténtica Guerra Civil en el Manchester United
articles.summary: Las declaraciones de Lisandro Martínez contra la directiva han desatado una auténtica Guerra Civil en el Manchester United
articles.body: Las palabras de Lisandro Martínez tras la derrota del United por 2-0 contra el Atlético de Madrid ha desatado una auténtica guerra civil en Mánchester. Su compañero Amand Diallo ha calificado la situación del Manchester United como de "una puta vergüenza", los analistas lo definen como "un barco que se hunde" y leyendas como Wayne Rooney, Jamie Carragher, Ashley Young o Paul Robinson cargaron contra el defensa argentino. Amad Diallo, compañero de Lisandro Martínez en el Manchester United, publicó una reacción contundente en Snapchat tras la derrota contra el Atlético de Madrid. El futbolista calificó la situación actual del Manchester United como una "puta vergüenza, no tengo palabras". Wayne Rooney, leyenda del Manchester United, ha criticado duramente la airada reacción de Lisandro Martínez. El mítico goleador acusó al defensa argentino de tener una "intención oculta" durante su entrevista posterior al partido, en la que Lisandro Martínez arremetió contra la directiva de los 'diablos rojos' y el director técnico Jason Wilcox. Wayne Rooney considera que Lisandro Martínez ha corrido el riesgo de generar más caos en el vestuario del Manchester United y de alterar la armonía con sus compañeros de equipo. "Es una situación complicada, porque yo siempre fui de expresar lo que pensaba cuando era jugador y es natural querer dar tu opinión, pero creo que quizás él ha ido demasiado lejos. Eso es algo que le corresponde al entrenador y que debería mantenerse en el ámbito interno; los aficionados quieren escuchar a los jugadores y ver que realmente les importa el equipo, comentó el exfubolista de 40 años en 'Amazon Prime'. Rooney subrayó que "está claro que a Lisandro Martínez le importa y quiere que el club invierta más dinero y fiche a más jugadores; aunque, siendo sincero, si eso sucede, creo que él podría ser uno de los primeros en salir debido a su propio rendimiento. Su nivel de juego no ha sido lo suficientemente bueno, pero creo que en cierto modo tiene razón: el club necesita invertir más tanto en la zona de ataque como en la defensa". "Creo que lo de Lisandro Martínez fue algo muy premeditado. ¿Por qué concede la entrevista justo después de este partido? ¿Se ofreció él mismo? Rara vez le oigo hablar. Parecía algo planeado, algo que había comentado con su equipo antes de hacerlo público. Es triste, porque cuando necesitas que todos los jugadores permanezcan unidos, no puedes andar aireando lo que sucede en la directiva. Me parece que Lisandro tenía una intención oculta, porque eso no se corresponde con la actuación. Yo creo que la actuación fue mejor... Creo que también es un tanto irrespetuoso con sus compañeros, ya que les falta al respeto al dar a entender que no tienen el nivel suficiente", apuntó. Wayne Rooney insistió en que "la directiva tiene que analizar esto y probablemente deba tomar medidas al respecto, porque es una falta de respeto hacia todo el club. Sí, hay problemas; todo el mundo quiere más jugadores y mejores jugadores, pero estos son los que tienes. Como jugador, tienes que seguir adelante. Tienes que salir y demostrar por qué eres campeón del mundo". "Para ser sincero, no creo que Lisandro Martínez haya logrado conectar realmente con los aficionados desde que llegó, ya que ha sufrido muchas lesiones. La verdad es que me gusta, creo que es un buen jugador, pero ha estado lesionado; así que, teniendo en cuenta lo que el Manchester United pagó por él, no ha rendido lo esperado. Dicho esto, no pretendo faltar al respeto; simplemente creo que ha tenido muchas lesiones y no ha jugado tanto", comentó. Jamie Carragher, leyenda del Liverpool y célebre comentarista televisivo, también se pronunció sobre las palabras de Lisandro Martínez contra la directiva del Manchester United. "No benefician a nadie en absoluto; ahora ellos serán el centro de atención durante los próximos días debido a esto. A ninguna afición le gustan los directivos ni los jefes de arriba, así que los seguidores del United se lo tragarán encantados y les parecerá genial", comentó en 'CBS Sports'. Jamie Carragher subrayó que "me parece fatal que Lisandro Martínez haya salido a decir eso. Cuando afirma que 'tuvimos una temporada fantástica' la campaña pasada... no fue así; de hecho, despidieron al entrenador. Terminaron terceros porque no jugaron partidos de copa ni competiciones europeas, ya que quedaron eliminados de los torneos de copa muy pronto". "La razón por la que no ficharon jugadores en verano es que, en los cuatro o cinco años que lleva allí, creo que sólo se han clasificado para la Champions League una vez. Así que, si cada temporada te quedas sin los ingresos de la Champions mientras el Manchester United gasta más de 200 millones de euros en el mercado de fichajes, tarde o temprano eso tiene que parar, porque el dinero no está ahí. Por eso, el dinero que el Manchester United está desembolsando este verano corresponde a jugadores comprados hace años; de ahí que no haya fondos disponibles, pues no se puede seguir así indefinidamente. Es una plantilla que ha pasado por distintos entrenadores y ha rendido fatal; esta noche han vuelto a jugar de forma pésima", apuntó. Carragher resaltó que "Lisandro Martínez ha tenido un inicio de temporada pésimo; pésimo, realmente malo". "La temporada pasada, Ruben Amorim arremetió contra sus superiores, y yo dije de inmediato que debían despedirlo, y no solo por esos comentarios. Yo pensaba: 'Tienes suerte de conservar el puesto; no puedes ponerte a criticar a quienes están por encima de ti'. Creo que un club de fútbol es una familia y que hay muchas cosas sucediendo en su interior: hay discusiones, hay gente descontenta... Puedo entender que él no esté satisfecho con la plantilla —o que Michael Carrick tampoco lo esté—, pero hay que considerar al club en su conjunto", reflexionó el ídolo de los 'reds'. Ashley Young, otro mítico exjugador del Manchester United, se hizo eco de las palabras de Wayne Rooney contra Lisandro Martínez y ratificó que los comentarios del argentino complicarían la situación del entrenador Carrick en los próximos días. "Por supuesto, es un tema del que hablan los jugadores. Antes del partido hablábamos de que el club necesitaba invertir más, pero... han invertido en el centro del campo, así que ¿qué es lo que él quiere? ¿Que compren un equipo totalmente nuevo? No van a hacer eso. Necesitan reforzar otras posiciones. Podrían haber fichado jugadores para la delantera o la defensa, pero no lo hicieron. Acaba de terminar el partido y las emociones están a flor de piel; eso lo entendemos. Pero sabemos que los fichajes deben funcionar y mejorar; el club debe tomarse su tiempo para hacerlo bien", comentó el exfutbolista. Ashley Young cree que "los jugadores deben asumir su responsabilidad: 'somos nosotros quienes formamos este equipo y esta plantilla, y somos nosotros quienes salimos al campo'. Son ellos quienes deben rendir y demostrar de qué son capaces. No habrá cambios hasta enero". Paul Robinson, ex portero de Inglaterra, se expresó en BBC Radio 5 Live sobre las controvertidas declaraciones de Lisandro Martínez: "Cuestiono el momento elegido, con todo el revuelo que hay actualmente en torno al Manchester United; es necesario que salga una actitud positiva del vestuario, pero es evidente que no han fichado bien, que necesitan más jugadores y que la plantilla no es lo suficientemente fuerte". Jason Cundy ha calificado esta reacción de Lisandro Martínez como una mentalidad de "barco que se hunde", acusando a los jugadores del Manchester United egoísmo por trasladar la culpa a los propietarios en lugar de asumir la responsabilidad de una temporada desastrosa. En Sky Sports señalaron que los jugadores que critican públicamente a la directiva, estableciendo paralelismos con el caso de Cristiano Ronaldo en 2022, suelen durar poco en Old Trafford, especialmente teniendo en cuenta que Martínez se encuentra actualmente en el último año de su contrato. Después de la derrota del Manchester Unite por 2-0 contra el Atlético de Madrid el argentino Lisandro Martínez apuntó a los despachos de Old Trafford: "No se puede estar cambiando, cambiando y cambiando de entrenador. ¿Qué pasa con otras áreas? Esta noche es fácil hablar del entrenador, es fácil hablar de los jugadores, pero también tenemos que fijarnos en otros aspectos". "Hemos hecho un partido realmente pobre. Realmente pobre. Tengo que controlarme mucho, pero a veces es un reflejo de cómo está nuestro club en este momento. Espero más inversión. Al 100%. Espero más de nuestro director técnico. Tengo que ser honesto, como jugadores tenemos que hacer más, pero también es importante, cuando tienes un equipo fuerte, estar preparado para una noche como esta", dijo el argentino en Amazon Prime. Lisandro Martínez insistió en la idea de que "tuvimos una temporada fantástica el año pasado y ahora esperamos más de la directiva, de los altos mandos, para que traigan más jugadores para competir, porque muchos equipos también han fichado a muchos jugadores".

articles.title: Raúl Varela: "Al fútbol se juega a lo que diga Lamine"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de La Tribu destaca la superioridad del futbolista del Barcelona tras su exhibición ante el Galatasaray y lanza un mensaje al Real Madrid
articles.summary: El presentador de La Tribu destaca la superioridad del futbolista del Barcelona tras su exhibición ante el Galatasaray y lanza un mensaje al Real Madrid
articles.body: Raúl Varela ha dedicado su reflexión en La Tribu a Lamine Yamal, protagonista de una nueva exhibición del Barcelona en la Liga de Campeones. El periodista, que fue crítico con el rendimiento del internacional español durante el Mundial, no ha escatimado elogios hacia el azulgrana después de su actuación ante el Galatasaray. "No seré yo sospechoso de juzgar a Lamine Yamal cuando nada más acabar el Mundial califiqué su actuación como discreta tirando a mala", comenzó recordando Varela, que situó al futbolista por detrás de otros protagonistas de la selección española: "Entre las estrellas, claramente de los menos destacados, y a nivel de selección campeona del mundo, por detrás de otros futbolistas como Rodri, Cubarsi, Oyarzabal o Unai Simón". Sin embargo, el director de La Tribu considera que el presente del jugador azulgrana merece un reconocimiento rotundo: "Pero se puede decir todo esto y se debe decir también que hoy por hoy al fútbol se juega a lo que diga Lamine". Varela puso como ejemplo lo sucedido en Estambul, donde el Barcelona volvió a sumar una victoria europea gracias, en buena medida, al talento de su joven estrella. "Que tiene la tarde regular, pues el Barça se va al descanso empatando a uno ante el Galatasaray. Que se le parece una broma de mal gusto lo de no ganar en Estambul, pues un regate aquí, una asistencia allá y la décima victoria que cae como una fila de fichas de dominó que se empujan unas a las otras", explicó. El periodista también destacó el extraordinario momento de forma del internacional español, que ya había dejado muestras de su calidad durante el parón de selecciones: "Todo esto después de un parón de selecciones en el que en apenas diez minutos de competición fue capaz de meter tres goles. En Wembley, en el Pizjuán y en el Tartiere". Para Varela, el nivel mostrado por Lamine invita a pensar en las posibilidades del Barcelona en Europa: "Su superioridad es manifiesta y ayer presentó el aval con su Barcelona para que Europa, esta vez sí, pueda estar a su alcance". La reflexión del director de La Tribu también tuvo espacio para el Real Madrid y José Mourinho, especialmente por la polémica arbitral que rodea al conjunto blanco. "Veremos si toman nota en Madrid que ha trasladado el debate arbitral hasta Roma en la previa de un partido incómodo para Mourinho en un lugar donde fue feliz", señaló Varela. Y cerró su intervención con una comparación entre las palabras del técnico madridista y la actuación del joven futbolista del Barcelona: "Mou nos pidió que viésemos el primer minuto ante el Villarreal para entender muchas cosas. Yo lo que vi fue al Tete, creo que así le llama a Lamine su hermano Keyne, ante el Galata. Con ese nivel de juego, al Barça no lo para ni Negreira".

articles.title: Qué pasó en Mestalla... un 14 de octubre: la riada de 1957 y el estadio anegado por completo de agua
articles.standfirst: Fue una de las noches más trágicas que vivió la ciudad inundándola toda y Mestalla no fue excepción: ahora bien, actuó de refugio con sus gradas para evitar mayor tragedia humana
articles.summary: Fue una de las noches más trágicas que vivió la ciudad inundándola toda y Mestalla no fue excepción: ahora bien, actuó de refugio con sus gradas para evitar mayor tragedia humana
articles.body: Un 14 de octubre siempre es una fecha recordada en Valencia. Por las lluvias torrenciales que provocaron que el antiguo cauce del río Turia, que pasa por en medio de la capital valenciana, se viera desbordado y dejara toda la ciudad inundada. Mestalla tampoco se libró. El agua llegó a una altura impactante tal y como se ve reflejado en los distintos registros fotográficos del pasado... y del presente a día de hoy. El campo, ubicado cerca del viejo cauce, sufrió graves daños materiales, pero al mismo tiempo desempeñó un papel humano conmovedor como refugio de salvación para cientos de vecinos del barrio. Sus gradas fueron la tabla de salvación de muchos. La fuerza del agua inundó por completo las instalaciones, dejando el terreno de juego totalmente impracticable... lugar donde no se pudo jugar durante mucho tiempo. Po todo ello, el Valencia se vio obligado a seguir la competición pero lo hizo jugando lejos de Mestalla. Encadenó hasta cinco partidos seguidos como visitante mientras la ciudad y el estadio intentaban recuperarse de la catástrofe. De hecho, existe una placa conmemorativa instalada por el club en la zona de los vestuarios que es la zona más profunda que hay del estadio donde queda reflejada la altura a la que llegó el agua. Esta marca indica el asombroso e imponente nivel que alcanzaron las aguas negras dentro del propio recinto blanquinegro. Mestalla se convirtió en parte esencial de aquel momento tan crítico vivido en la ciudad con la riada del 57. Mestalla se convirtió en refugio aquella noche fatídica... Los cuerpos de seguridad y bomberos evacuaron a multitud de familias cuyas viviendas corrían peligro, y se utilizaron las gradas altas y los accesos del estadio como zona segura para pasar la noche y protegerse de la corriente de agua. Aquella noche trágica en la capital se cobró la vida de 81 personas, pero el balance humano de la riada fue trágico... Se sospecha que el número real pudo ser mayor, llegando hasta 300 víctimas mortales.

articles.title: UEFA Champions League Matchday 2 Predictions Including PSG at Manchester City
articles.summary: Nine matches on Wednesday will conclude matchday 2 of the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League. We have an Iberian clash between Porto and Real Betis to preview, al...
articles.body:
Nine matches on Wednesday will conclude matchday 2 of the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League. We have an Iberian clash between Porto and Real Betis to preview, along with PSG at Manchester City. The other set of predictions covers matches for Liverpool and Real Madrid. Here's your look at another European night to savour.

UEFA Champions League Wednesday Predictions

Real Betis aren't just plucky underdogs anymore, they are one of the best teams in La Liga and playing at home, they should be able to challenge a strong Porto side that have 24 points from 8 games in Portugal and lead the league by 5 points already. Porto's Polish wall of Jan Bednarek and Jakub Kiwior is one of the best in Europe, while Gabri Veiga, a 24-year-old Spaniard, has scored four times domestically. Bednarek is suspended for this one, and William Gomes is out too.

Betis dominated Osasuna on the weekend winning 5-2, their top rated outfield player is defender Marc Bartra, but Antony and Isco are pure-class too. Antony and Junior Firpo have fitness questions, but Troy Parrott can step up in the forward line for Betis.

Porto can play cagey, controlled football but Betis at home has been one of the most fun environments in Europe over the last 12 months.

Slovan is at home but I'm not sold on their quality as PSG hammered them 6-1 and they drew against Skalica on the weekend. Slovenian international Andraz Sporar is their top scorer at 32-years-old. Stuttgart beat Paderborn on the weekend to return to winning ways after a poor domestic start. Defender Maximilian Mittelstadt has been their standout, but he's injured for this one, as is Luca Jaquez and a couple of other first-choice players.

Still, Stuttgart look to be a level up compared to Bratislava, who may struggle to get points this UCL League season.

Two of the best teams from the lower leagues of Europe. AEK Athens are second in Greece with Barnabas Varga having scored freely. The trouble for Athens is he's expected to be out of this matchup. Shakhtar, playing in London at Stamford Bridge, will get Pedrinho back from an injury but may miss Marlon Santos. Kaua Elias is their best attacker. This is a pretty even matchup, but Donetsk's Brazilian attack could shine and give them enough for all three points.

The off-field drama around the future of Manchester City hasn't dented their on-field form, as they top the Premier League and haven't lost. PSG have stumbled in Ligue 1, but remain Europe's Champions and a great team presently, including the derby win away in Marseille. Ferran Torres, ex Manchester City, is now a key man at PSG as they are retooled and reloaded for another Championship chase. Erling Haaland, one goal from the club's all-time UCL scoring record, and City move the ball around and create goalscoring chances as well. Both squads are nearly fit, it's a titanic clash, but at the Etihad it's advantage City on form alone.

Aston Villa know how to score but they concede going the other way just as much this season. Villa's win over Club Brugge looks impressive now, while they drew Brentford on the weekend in the Premier League. John McGinn and Nicolas Jackson being two of the players to watch for the hosts. Leon Goretzka's fitness is a slight concern , while Ian Maatsen is still out.

Fenerbahce had an 8-0 win over Eyupspor in the domestic league on September 20th and currently sport the best goal difference in Turkiye. Mason Greenwood and Ederson have been among the standouts. This match is ultimately another test of the Premier League's quality .

Playing at Villa Park, I expect the home side to be the one that emerges with the points.

articles.body:
The Champions League is enjoying a whirlwind week, with Spanish clubs taking center stage amid goal-filled displays, emotional victories and build-ups dominated by refereeing controversy.

Barça run riot as Atlético celebrate an emotional win

Barcelona and Atlético Madrid passed their European tests with flying colors. Hansi Flick's side produced a superb second half to thrash Galatasaray 4-1 in Istanbul. Meanwhile, Atlético dedicated an emotional 2-0 victory over Manchester United to captain Koke, while Villarreal secured a hugely valuable win in their European campaign.

Mourinho turns up the heat ahead of Madrid clash

All eyes are on the Stadio Olimpico today, where Real Madrid visit Roma. The clash comes amid the fallout from José Mourinho's explosive remarks on Italian television, where he fiercely criticized recent refereeing in Spain and reignited the controversy surrounding the Negreira case just hours before kickoff.

Elsewhere, the European fixtures produced results that defied predictions. Bayern Munich salvaged a dramatic 3-3 draw away to Norway's Viking after falling 2-0 behind in the opening minutes. Inter Milan suffered the biggest setback, losing 4-3 to Club Brugge at San Siro, while Arsenal comfortably dispatched Lille 3-0.

In women's football, Spain ended their American tour by conceding a 2-2 draw against the United States. Sonia Bermúdez's side went 2-0 up, but the hosts rallied late on to level the match. Spain thus conclude their international preparations with mixed feelings after letting a commanding lead slip.

The Americas' most prestigious tournament raises the curtain on its semifinals today with the big São Paulo derby between Fluminense and Palmeiras in the Copa Libertadores. Meanwhile, the Copa Sudamericana got underway last night with bad news for Argentine fans, as Boca Juniors lost 1-0 to Vasco da Gama at La Bombonera.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal reveals what he called his stunning assist in Barcelona’s 4-1 Galatasaray win
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal once again proved decisive for Barcelona, earning the Man of the Match award after producing two assists in their 4-1 Champions League victory o...
articles.body:
Lamine Yamal once again proved decisive for Barcelona, earning the Man of the Match award after producing two assists in their 4-1 Champions League victory over Galatasaray in Istanbul.

The Barcelona winger created the goals for Fermin Lopez and Anthony Gordon early in the second half, helping Hansi Flick's side turn a difficult away fixture into a commanding win.

However, it was his remarkable piece of skill before setting up Gordon that caught particular attention.

Lamine explains his stunning assist against Galatasaray

Asked to explain the moment, Yamal gave it a characteristically relaxed description while making it clear that the outcome mattered more than the technique.

"What would I call that move? I don't know. I'd call it an 'almost rabona.' The important thing is that it worked out well for the assist to Gordon—it was effective," he explained.

Yamal continued to search for a goal of his own throughout the match, repeatedly asking his teammates for the ball even as the final whistle approached.

Although he failed to get on the scoresheet, his contribution showed why he remains such a central figure in Barcelona's attacking plans.

His ability to beat defenders in one-on-one situations, create openings and find teammates in dangerous positions gave Galatasaray persistent problems.

Notably, Yamal's two assists against Galatasaray took his tally to four in this season's Champions League, making him the competition's leading assist provider at the time of the report.

UEFA recognised his contribution by awarding him the Man of the Match prize, highlighting the two assists and his outstanding piece of skill.

Lamine earns admiration in Istanbul after Barcelona win

Yamal also acknowledged the challenge Barcelona faced against Galatasaray, particularly given the atmosphere inside the Turkish club's home stadium.

"We knew it was a very tough stadium, and one of the most challenging places we can play.

"We were talking about it in the locker room—about the way they press and cheer. We're very happy with the victory. They're a quality team."

Lastly, when asked if Barcelona can win the treble this season, his response was emphatic, stating, "Always. We're Barcelona, we're the best team in the world."

Meanwhile, the winger attracted considerable attention after the match, with supporters and families seeking photographs.

On that note, Galatasaray forward Victor Osimhen stopped him on the way to the dressing room to request a picture with his sister, while Yamal also took a photograph with Osimhen and his children.

Barcelona left Istanbul with three important points, while Yamal's performance offered another reminder of his growing influence on the European stage.

Four assists in the competition so far have made him a major creative threat, and his display against Galatasaray showed why opponents continue to struggle to contain him.

articles.title: Arsenal Learn Martin Zubimendi Fate After Undergoing Tests
articles.summary: Arsenal have learnt the extent of Martin Zubimendi's recent injury, after undergoing scans this week.
articles.body:
Arsenal midfielder Martin Zubimendi has avoided a serious injury after undergoing a scan on the ankle problem he picked up following the victory over Leeds United , according to Mikel Arteta

The scan revealed a minor issue, with the Spaniard only expected to miss a matter of days.

Zubimendi was an unused substitute in the comeback win over Leeds last Saturday, the first time he failed to feature for Arsenal since January. Having not played, he took part in a post-match warm-down at the Emirates, where he sustained the injury during a small-sided game.

Piero Hincapié was also hurt in the same session, and both players were ruled out of the Champions League clash with Lille.

The Ecuadorian suffered a more severe injury than his Spanish teammate, with Hincapié now sidelined for a matter of weeks.

Mikel Arteta defended the decision to hold the session in his pre-match press conference, though he admitted he would ask his players to be more careful in future.

He said, 'What we can do is say, "Guys, they are so competitive, when we do that, please don't touch each other too much," to avoid these kind of things.'

The setback comes at a frustrating time for Zubimendi, who has struggled for regular minutes since the latter stages of last season. After making 57 appearances in all competitions in his debut campaign, he lost his place to Myles Lewis-Skelly during the title run-in, starting just one of the final six league games.

His only start this season came in the Carabao Cup third-round win at Ipswich Town, where he recorded an assist.

The 27-year-old joined Arsenal from Real Sociedad in July 2025 in a deal worth around £51million, with the Gunners fending off a late effort from Real Madrid, a year after Zubimendi had turned down Liverpool.

He could return as soon as the weekend as Arsenal travel to Nottingham Forest, giving Arteta another option in midfield.

The Spanish boss explained after Arsenal's victory over Lille that the midfielder was 'much, much better', a boost to the Gunners ahead of a busy period.

Arsenal are well stocked in the midfield department, with Declan Rice, Martin Ødegaard and Lewis-Skelly the first-choice trio, whilst Bruno Guimarães has impressed off the bench, scoring the opener at Sunderland last month, and the winner against Leeds on Saturday.

With Lewis-Skelly reverting to full-back following Hincapié's injury, Zubimendi is presented with an opportunity to stake his claim in the middle of the park in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta Reveals Bukayo Saka Battled Through Illness After Starring in Lille Victory
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta revealed that Bukayo Saka battled through illness to provide an assist for Eberechi Eze before scoring Arsenal’s third goal in their 3-0 win ove...
articles.body:
The 25-year-old had started all but one of Arsenal' s games across all competitions this season, but was named on the bench for the Champions League clash before coming on to make an immediate impact.

"I'm very happy and welcome. He wasn't feeling that good yesterday and today because he had a sort of illness," Arteta explained.

"He wasn't ready to start, but he really was keen to contribute to the team if it was needed. He came on, he made a huge impact and he delivered with real quality."

Jurrien Timber opened the scoring before Arsenal struck twice more in a seven-minute spell of dominance to put the game beyond Lille 's reach.

Despite the hosts enjoying plenty of possession in the first half, the game was still finely balanced until Arteta responded aptly with a triple substitution.

Saka had been on the pitch for just two minutes before setting up Eze for the second goal, while his own strike capped another well-worked team move. Some excellent interplay between the England international, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz created the opportunity for the Arsenal winger to slot past Berke Ozer from close range.

The goal came just days after Arteta publicly challenged Saka to improve his goalscoring output, with the Arsenal manager opting to reveal the exchange he had with the winger following his pre-match press conference.

"After the press conference I went and he was at the massage table and I said, 'Bukayo, I just killed you in the press conference. Good luck tomorrow.'

"He was laughing. He knows me. He knows that we have discussed these kinds of things. He takes it because he wants to be the best version of himself."

His comments highlight the close relationship between the pair, with the Arsenal manager setting things straight that his challenge was intended to help rather than place any further unnecessary pressure on the 25-year-old.

The England international seemed to take to the challenge, responding on the pitch by contributing directly to two goals, despite not feeling well enough to start.

Saka's strike takes his tally up to four goals this season, looking to build on his performances after a disappointing campaign last season.

However, his eagerness to rise up to the challenge will undoubtedly be viewed as an encouraging sign as the Gunners continue to fight on all fronts in every competition.

articles.title: Newcastle Send Scouts To Monitor Valencia Winger David Otorbi
articles.summary: The Magpies are tracking Valencia’s teenage sensation after a breakout performance in Spain, eyeing the 18-year-old attacker as a priority for their long-ter...
articles.body:
Newcastle United have reportedly sent scouts to Spain to monitor the progress of Valencia winger David Otorbi, with the highly rated teenager attracting renewed attention following an impressive performance in La Liga.

According to reports in Spain, Newcastle representatives were present at El Sardinero on Sunday to watch the 18-year-old in action during Valencia's 2-2 draw against Racing Santander. The young attacker made a significant impact after coming off the bench, scoring his first senior goal for Valencia before coming close to creating a late winner.

The scouting mission suggests the Magpies are continuing to assess emerging attacking talent as they look to identify potential additions for the future. However, there has been no confirmation of a formal bid or an agreement between the two clubs.

Newcastle Continue To Assess Young Talent

Newcastle's reported interest in Otorbi comes amid ongoing attention on recruitment and the development of the club's attacking options.

The Magpies' scouting department must balance the need for immediate first-team quality with identifying younger players who could become valuable assets over several seasons. Recruitment at this stage can provide clubs with opportunities to secure promising talent before their reputation and transfer value increase significantly.

Otorbi's age and experience mean that any potential move would need to be considered carefully. Newcastle would have to assess whether he could contribute immediately, develop within the club's existing structure or benefit from further experience before becoming a regular first-team option.

Valencia, meanwhile, have a clear incentive to retain control of a player they have developed through their academy. The club announced a contract extension in April 2026, with the agreement running until 2028 and a further extension option reported. Spanish reports have also indicated that Otorbi would prefer to continue his development at Valencia rather than rush into a move elsewhere.

That situation could make negotiations complicated if Newcastle decide to turn their interest into a concrete approach.

For now, the reported scouting trip should be viewed as an assessment of a promising young player rather than evidence that a transfer is imminent.

Newcastle have yet to publicly confirm their interest, and there is no verified indication that an offer has been submitted. Further monitoring could follow if Otorbi continues to impress with his performances for Valencia.

His latest display has nevertheless provided a timely reminder of his potential. Scoring his first senior goal and nearly creating a winner in the same appearance is an encouraging return for a young winger seeking to establish himself.

Whether Newcastle pursue the Spaniard in a future transfer window remains to be seen, but his name is now firmly linked with the club's recruitment activity.

If the Magpies believe Otorbi has the potential to develop into a high-level Premier League winger, continued scouting could be the first step towards a more serious assessment of his availability.

For now, Newcastle supporters will have to wait for further developments to discover whether this reported interest progresses beyond the scouting stage.

articles.title: “Very soft”: Wayne Rooney bemoans key moment that turned match away from Man United in defeat to Atletico Madrid
articles.summary: Manchester United fell to a 0-2 loss to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday night in the Champions League.The matchIt was the club’s first defeat in Europe this seaso...
articles.body:
Manchester United fell to a 0-2 loss to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday night in the Champions League.

It was the club's first defeat in Europe this season, but their fourth overall in what has been a very concerning start to the campaign.

In the side's latest display of defensive vulnerability, they conceded a goal after just 47 seconds to Pablo Barrios.

United did fight their way back into the game, and Bryan Mbeumo, Carlos Baleba and Bruno Fernandes were all guilty of missing big chances in the match.

The game took a final decisive turn when Leny Yoro was sent off after a VAR intervention, as he was judged to have brought down Jonathan David as the last man.

Shortly after, Ademola Lookman added the hosts' second and the game was over as a contest.

Former Manchester United star Wayne Rooney did see some positives for the Red Devils in spite of another negative result for Michael Carrick's side.

Speaking on Amazon Prime in comments carried by The Athletic , Rooney stated, "I thought it was better tonight. The result is disappointing but there were positive signs."

The club's all-time record goalscorer made sure to praise new signing Carlos Baleba, who was making his first start for the club.

Rooney explained, "Baleba coming in was excellent and added that extra energy and Santos did well in there as well so overall I thought there were more positives."

The pundit also felt United were unlucky to go down to ten men. The former striker asserted, "the red card was very soft and probably wasn't a red card and the game was done then."

United will hope to carry this positivity into their next match with Leeds United on Sunday.

articles.title: Lisandro Martinez rips into Manchester United board after disappointing Champions League loss
articles.summary: Lisandro Martinez launched a scathing attack on the Manchester United board after Tuesday’s 2-0 loss at Atletico Madrid.The Red Devils produced a much-improv...
articles.body:
Lisandro Martinez launched a scathing attack on the Manchester United board after Tuesday's 2-0 loss at Atletico Madrid .

The Red Devils produced a much-improved performance at the Metropolitano Stadium following the disappointing home draw against Tottenham Hotspur.

But individual errors meant they had to return empty handed from the away Champions League fixture.

The result has piled pressure on head coach Michael Carrick whose team is now on a five-game winless run.

Talking to the media after the match, Martinez called out the club's technical director Jason Wilcox for not supporting Carrick in the transfer market.

He said: "I expect more [investment]. 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox].

"I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night."

United endured a disappointing summer transfer window .

The club failed to bring in striking support for Benjamin Sesko and competition at left-back for Luke Shaw.

They spent around £155 million to sign Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba.

Elliot Anderson, Mateus Fernandes and Aurelien Tchouameni were their primary midfield targets but missed out on all of them.

United refused to pay an exorbitant fee for these stars, with the club's transfer policy changed under INEOS.

But their cautious approach in the market means the club is struggling for quality in their squad. Their performances on the pitch this season have been massively underwhelming.

Man United are currently 13th in the Premier League, having won just one of their six matches.

articles.title: Lisandro Martinez’s extraordinary rant told the truth about Man United’s inept hierarchy
articles.summary: MANCHESTER UNITED IN CRISIS... AGAIN: Comment: Martinez pointed the finger at the club’s board after Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid – and Chris W...
articles.body:
After a summer that promised so much, Manchester United have arrived in an autumn of discontent. Just as it looked like they might be turning a corner, they're back to square one.

Tuesday's Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid may well put Michael Carrick on the brink of losing his job. Several United players – notably captain Bruno Fernandes – looked totally dejected at full-time – and that was before Lisandro Martinez decided to launch an astonishing attack on the club's ownership .

The result leaves United with just two wins from their opening nine games of the season, with those coming against newly promoted Ipswich and Champions League debutants Sabah. It is a far cry from the team that won 12 of their last 17 Premier League games on their way to finishing third last term.

"Sometimes it's a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment, you know?" Martinez said to Prime Video in Madrid. "We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top. I expect more, 100 per cent. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]."

It was a surprising tirade from the Argentine, though one most United fans will agree with. And while it signals real discontent among the players, Carrick was quick to emphasise how together the squad is in terms of matters on the pitch. The players clearly back their manager too, with Martinez saying that United "can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager".

While Carrick's tactics and his role in United's downturn in form will rightly face scrutiny , it's clear that this is not an issue of a player revolt against the manager, but rather disillusionment over the actions of those at the top of the club.

This will hurt Ineos and the likes of Wilcox and director of recruitment Christopher Vivell, mostly because Martinez is undeniably correct. United spent a portion of the summer pursuing Elliot Anderson, only to see him move to rivals Manchester City, while they instead signed Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba for a combined total of around £150m for a different type of midfield rebuild.

A few weeks later, only Baleba looks up to the required standard. Spending £50m on Santos – a player who could not get regular starts for Chelsea – when other parts of the squad needed investment now looks staggeringly inept – especially if Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko are injured.

United did not invest in a forward despite plenty of evidence that Joshua Zirkzee is not good enough for their ambitions, and they failed in their pursuit of Lewis Hall, leaving themselves with only one recognised left-back in the squad.

The rest of the defence was an afterthought, with reports emerging that the hierarchy are planning a defensive rebuild next summer. It would appear a naive approach. You can't expect every signing to work out, but this strategy simply suggests that some key people do not know how to run a football club.

That is the core complaint from Martinez, with others – notably Fernandes – also seemingly frustrated at the start of this season. You suspect Carrick and certain players were given assurances over investment into the squad, and yet United spent just £163m over the summer, which is less than all of their top six rivals, as well as newly-promoted clubs Hull and Ipswich.

To make matters worse, the atmosphere has soured off the pitch too, with the recent season ticketing fiasco causing a further rift between the hierarchy and fans, who feel that they've been treated unfairly. Bans are now extending to members. While some touts will be scuppered in this new drive, innocent fans are also getting caught out with limited time to appeal and a lack of clarity regarding what exactly has led to the accusations.

That a job advert for a "Supporter Escalations Executive" – to "support the Club's mission to tackle ticket touting" – was not filled before a huge number of investigations and bans highlights the confused, haphazard nature of work that has now characterised the club for at least the last 13 years, if not more.

Add to this the farce surrounding the hiring and firing of Dan Ashworth, as well as the cutting of 322 jobs, and Ineos are miles away from the best-in-class image they have tried to present to the outside world. It would be difficult to get away with this level of ineptitude in most other jobs.

There are mitigating factors, most notably the $1.1bn of debt lumped on the club by the Glazer family , but Ineos have not enamoured themselves with the fans, adding to the mess created by the Glazers over the last two decades or so. They are now in charge of much of the footballing side and they simply haven't delivered – now it's clear that the players are disillusioned too.

While Wayne Rooney was probably right in saying that Martinez's interview " is not going to help the situation ", it might be a case where things have to get worse before they get better.

There needs to be a reckoning at United, and while the Glazers should undeniably be at the top of the list when that time comes, a number of figures associated with the minority ownership also have uncomfortable questions to answer.

articles.title: Barcelona midfielder Pedri reveals why he asked to be substituted against Galatasaray: ‘Wasn’t feeling too well’
articles.summary: Pedri delivered another commanding performance as Barcelona defeated Galatasaray 4-1 in Istanbul, helping Hansi Flick’s side take control of their Champions...
articles.body:
Pedri delivered another commanding performance as Barcelona defeated Galatasaray 4-1 in Istanbul , helping Hansi Flick's side take control of their Champions League clash after falling behind.

The midfielder did not get on the scoresheet, but his influence was central to Barcelona's second-half response.

The Spain international was substituted in the closing minutes, prompting questions about his condition.

However, Pedri clarified after the match that he was not dealing with an injury, explaining that stomach discomfort was the reason behind his request to come off.

The victory also gave him an opportunity to address Barcelona's attacking form ahead of a demanding run of fixtures against Real Betis, Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid.

Pedri explains why Barcelona struggled in the first half

Barcelona dominated possession for long periods against Galatasaray but struggled to make their control count before the break.

Pedri believes the team's decision-making in the final third was a key reason they failed to create more clear-cut opportunities.

"I think in the first half we were often too hasty with the final pass. We had the ball and saw plenty of space, but we were taking risks with the final pass.

"We should have kept it moving and let the forwards get involved, as we did in the second half. When players up front like Lamine, Fermin, Olmo or Gordon get the ball, they're decisive."

Galatasaray's opening goal made the task more difficult in front of their home supporters, but Barcelona responded with an emphatic second-half display.

"When Galatasaray take the lead in this atmosphere, it's tricky, but I'll take the team's reaction. The second half was spectacular."

Pedri addresses substitution and attacking form

Pedri also explained why he left the pitch late in the game, making clear that the decision was not related to a muscular problem or another injury.

"My stomach was hurting and I wasn't feeling too well. It was better to ask to be taken off and let someone else come on to freshen things up," he explained.

The midfielder was equally confident when discussing Barcelona's attacking output.

Flick's side had scored 43 goals in their first 10 competitive matches, offering a strong response to doubts about their finishing.

Pedri's performance was extremely underrated against Galatasaray. (Photo by Burak Kara/Getty Images)

"We're very confident. There was talk about us lacking a goal-scoring touch, but we're proving that this squad has it. It's only the start of the season; let's keep going.

"I think there's always speculation, but it's clear we can score plenty of goals.

"We've got plenty of quality players who also come off the bench. The squad is very deep and very good. You can see that," he explained.

Pedri looks ahead to Barcelona's crucial fixture run

Barcelona's victory in Istanbul was an important result, but Pedri knows the team face a significant test of their consistency over the coming weeks.

"We've got some very important matches coming up. It's early in the season, but they're important. Let's enjoy them and, above all, let's win," he concluded.

With Betis, PSG and Real Madrid next on the agenda, Barcelona will need Pedri's control and composure in midfield.

His performance against Galatasaray showed why he remains central to Flick's plans, while his assessment of the first half highlighted the fine margins the team must continue to improve, something that even Flick mentioned in his post-match comments .

articles.title: Kiat Lim le pide a su padre que no venda el Valencia
articles.standfirst: El hijo de Peter Lim está cómodo en la función de presidente y quiere ejercer en los próximos años
articles.summary: El hijo de Peter Lim está cómodo en la función de presidente y quiere ejercer en los próximos años
articles.body: Se ha hablado mucho de la venta del Valencia. Pero una realidad martilleante se repite una y otra vez: todos los que han intentado acercarse a Peter Lim con una oferta de compra del club han salido despedidos. Peter no ha movido ficha y la desesperación de la parroquia valencianista, que fue en aumento durante muchos años, se ha suavizado. El caso es que pese a los movimientos financieros del máximo mandatario, la venta de la parcela del viejo Mestalla, su reducción a mínimos del proyecto deportivo y la construcción del campo que estará lista para la próxima temporada, el escenario de venta parecía reflotar. "Lim prepara el club para venderlo", hemos leído y escuchado en muchas ocasiones. Sin embargo, MARCA ha podido saber que el hijo del máximo accionista le ha pedido a su padre que no venda el club.... al menos de momento. Kiat habló hace un par de semanas en Singapur con un ex directivo del Valencia y así se lo dijo. El actual presidente se siente cómodo en su cargo y quiere ejercer. Sus movimientos con la salida de Corberán, la llegada de Braulio y el fichaje de Aguirre le pusieron en primer plano en la toma de decisiones y su intención es seguir al frente del Consejo de Administración y llevar la 'empresa' de su padre a buen puerto. El hijo de Lim ha venido a Valencia en los últimos meses más veces que su padre desde que compró el club, empieza a recibir llamadas de gente de fútbol importante a nivel mundial y pese a la animadversión que sabe que existe en la ciudad contra su familia, quiere estar al frente y tomar decisiones. Obviamente la venta sigue estando encima de la mesa, pero ahora mismo Kiat ya ha hablado con su padre de no vender y la decisión, de momento es firme. En la conversación con el exdirectivo del club, Kiat habló de futuro y de las próximas temporadas, del equipo de trabajo y de los ingresos y posibilidades que abre el nuevo estadio con una masa de socios consolidada y una capacidad de negocio que puede aumentar de forma exponencial. El futuro del club sigue en manos de la familia Lim y de momento, Kiat, se hace fuerte con la bendición de su padre.

articles.title: Multiple Real Madrid insiders love Manchester City superstar who dreams of playing in Spain – report
articles.summary: Real Madrid have always attracted the biggest talents in the world and have had a pull unlike any other club in Europe.Their most successful eras have been b...
articles.body:
Real Madrid have always attracted the biggest talents in the world and have had a pull unlike any other club in Europe.

Their most successful eras have been built on generations of Galactico signings and finding systems that allow superstars to coexist.

Jose Mourinho is attempting to do the same right now, trying to bring silverware to a club that has Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Jude Bellingham.

Now, according to Le Journal du Real (h/t Madrid Zone ), Real Madrid are very interested in signing Manchester City superstar Erling Haaland.

Los Blancos ' admiration for the Norwegian is genuine, with Haaland himself said to be interested in playing in Spain at some point in his career.

Haaland remains an attractive option for Madrid

The 26-year-old striker has established himself among Europe's most feared goalscorers, combining exceptional physical strength with explosive movement and clinical finishing.

His ability to attack space behind defenders, dominate inside the penalty area and convert chances with minimal involvement makes him a particularly attractive option.

Erling Haaland dreams of playing in someday. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

For Madrid, interest in a player of Haaland's calibre is hardly surprising. The club has consistently sought elite attacking talent capable of defining an era.

However, admiration from people inside the club does not necessarily mean a transfer is being actively pursued.

Los Blancos are simply keeping an eye on the situation, considering everything going on around Manchester City and their 115 charges.

The most interesting question is not whether Haaland is good enough for Real Madrid, but how he would fit into a team already built around Kylian Mbappe.

Both players are devastating finishers, although their attacking qualities differ. Haaland operates as a conventional striker.

Mbappe, on the other hand, is more comfortable attacking space from different positions and carrying the ball towards goal.

Accommodating both in the same system is a nightmare for any tactician, even before factoring in the likes of Vinicius and Bellingham.

Madrid already possess considerable attacking quality, while recent performances have highlighted the need for better midfield progression and greater collective control.

Investing heavily in another superstar forward would make little sense if those structural weaknesses remained unresolved.

Could Haaland become Vinicius Jr.'s teammate at Real Madrid?. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

What Madrid need to spend money on is finally finding replacements for Toni Kroos and Luka Modric, who left a few seasons ago.

That does not diminish Haaland's appeal. A player of his quality would improve almost any attacking department.

Ultimately, if the opportunity presents itself, Madrid can consider a move for the Norwegian, but it cannot happen without sacrifices.

Right now, there is no basis to suggest that this transfer is imminent, and it remains to be seen what the future holds for Haaland and Manchester City.

articles.title: Farioli se queja del césped de La Cartuja: "No estará en muy buenas condiciones"
articles.standfirst: El técnico italiano del Oporto advierte de la dificultad del partido de hoy en La Cartuja
articles.summary: El técnico italiano del Oporto advierte de la dificultad del partido de hoy en La Cartuja
articles.body: El entrenador del Oporto, el italiano Francesco Farioli, destacó este martes en su rueda de prensa oficial previa al partido que el Betis, al que se medirán el miércoles en el Estadio La Cartuja en la segunda jornada de la fase de liga de la Champions, acumula "una racha impresionante de resultados". Una clara advertencia a sus futbolistas de la dificultad que entraña el encuentro. "Esperamos un equipo que, como nosotros, juegue de tú a tú y con ganas de ganar. El Betis está en un gran momento de forma y juega a un nivel altísimo en LaLiga", dijo Farioli en la sala de prensa del estadio sevillano, al que acudió con el equipo aunque no se entrenaron sobre el césped, que sí pisaron durante algunos minutos, porque lo hicieron por la mañana en la ciudad portuguesa. El técnico italiano elogió a su colega en el Betis, el chileno Manuel Pellegrini, quien lleva ya siete temporadas al frente de la plantilla verdiblanca y por ello "todos se conocen muy bien". Y apuntó del rival del conjunto portugués que tiene "mucha calidad en todas las posiciones, grandes jugadores individuales y mucha velocidad". "Es un partido que nos exigirá mucho y que daremos lo mejor de nosotros", dijo Farioli, quien comentó que todos los partidos de la 'Champions' "siempre son muy exigentes" y particularizó en que el de este miércoles se disputará en un terreno de juego que "no estará en muy buenas condiciones". "Estos pequeños detalles pueden afectar mental y físicamente a los jugadores, pero para eso hemos trabajado tan duro en la pretemporada, y por eso seguimos trabajando para que los jugadores estén en las mejores condiciones físicas y mentales, incluso compitiendo en tan poco tiempo", declaró el entrenador de Oporto, quien desveló que todavía tienen que "evaluar a algunos jugadores para poder decidir mañana por la mañana la alineación titular". "La ausencia de Bednarek es significativa. Tiene un gran impacto en el equipo, no solo en el rendimiento sino también en el liderazgo. Mañana tenemos ese problema, pero hemos logrado recuperar a Nehuén. Estuvo una semana completa con nosotros y está en plena forma", apuntó. Farioli puntualizó que cree que el miércoles "no importará quién esté en el campo" porque siempre encuentran "soluciones" y que todos "darán lo mejor de sí para jugar bien y brindar un momento feliz a los 3.500 aficionados (del Oporto) que estarán" en La Cartuja. También se refirió al mediapunta del conjunto verdiblanco Isco Alarcón, del que comentó que es "un jugador capaz de aportar creatividad al juego, una contribución muy importante con el balón en varios momentos y una enorme capacidad para generar superioridad numérica, pero el Betis tiene tres o cuatro extremos de élite, muy fuertes en el uno contra uno y con una gran capacidad de definición".

articles.title: Yamal magic helps Barcelona beat Galatasaray in Champions League
articles.summary: Yamal provided two assists and ‘turned the game around’ for Barcelona, who won 4-1 in Istanbul.
articles.body:
Barcelona and Lamine Yamal rediscovered their sparkle after a rocky first-half spell against Galatasaray to win 4-1 in their UEFA Champions League match in Turkiye.

Yamal tore the hosts apart after half-time at Istanbul’s Ali Sami Yen Stadium, Galatasaray’s cauldron, on Tuesday.

“It’s incredible to have players like that,” said Barcelona coach Hansi Flick of Yamal. “He’s turned the game around for us.”

Halfway through the second round of matches, the victory lifted Barcelona to the top of the Champions League table with two wins. Galatasaray are pointless and near the foot of the standings.

“We’re at a very high level. We have to keep going; the season is very long. We can’t relax,” Barcelona’s Fermin Lopez told a Spanish broadcaster.

Barcelona dominated the early stages. With Yamal vigorously policed on the right by the home defence, many of their attacks flowed through Anthony Gordon on the other flank.

Yet Galatasaray took the lead after 27 minutes. After Gordon went tumbling in the penalty box, the hosts launched a rapid counterattack through Rafael Leao on the left.

He pulled the ball back to the edge of the area to Russian Aleksey Batrakov, whose drive deflected off Joao Cancelo and into the corner of the goal.

“That goal made things a bit strange for us, because we had been dominating. But we knew how to react and come back,” said Fermin.

That ignited a spell of furious home pressure which culminated in Victor Osimhen rising to head a corner past goalkeeper Joan Garcia. Baris Yilmaz toed the ball over the line but was ruled offside.

Barcelona reasserted control. When Yamal went down on the edge of the box, the ball broke to a surprised Davinson Sanchez, who gave the ball away immediately. It fell to Dani Olmo, who threaded a pass to Cancelo, who scored.

At the start of the second half, Yamal took over. After setting up Gordon, who spurned the chance, he helped put Barca ahead in the 50th minute, placing a gentle curled cross on the forehead of Fermin, who nodded home.

“He’s a friend and a great teammate,” said Fermin of Yamal. “When he has the ball, I always look for a run. He’s the best in the world. We get along well off the field, and that shows on the pitch, too.”

Three minutes later, Yamal beat Eren Elmali three times, and in three different ways, in a tiny space before rolling a pass to Gordon in front of goal.

This time the England striker made no mistake, with Elmali, a Turkiye international, lifting his arms to the heavens in an expression of powerlessness.

After 65 minutes, Yamal cut in from his wing and fired a pass to replacement centre forward Gabriel Jesus. The ex-Arsenal man could not control the ball, but it deflected to Karim Adeyemi, who drilled the ball home.

“When you see the chances Lamine creates in every training session, it’s the same in matches,” said Flick. “I have a lot of top-quality players. Everyone’s watching Lamine – that’s only natural.”

Yamal could have scored himself, but after being quickest to a loose ball, he fired his shot over the bar.

The 19-year-old finished the game without a goal, which would have taken him closer to Kylian Mbappe’s record for Champions League goals as a teenager, but Yamal, who became Barcelona’s youngest-ever captain in the previous round, again took over the captain’s armband when Pedri was replaced.

articles.title: El palo del exjugador de la Roma al Real Madrid: "Siempre se quejan los que más se tienen que callar"
articles.standfirst: José Ángel Valdés 'Cote critica las protestas de los grandes clubes, cuestiona el juego del Real Madrid y reconoce que disfruta más viendo al Barcelona
articles.summary: José Ángel Valdés 'Cote critica las protestas de los grandes clubes, cuestiona el juego del Real Madrid y reconoce que disfruta más viendo al Barcelona
articles.body: José Ángel Valdés 'Cote' ha pasado por los micrófonos de La Tribu de Radio MARCA para charlar con Raúl Varela sobre la actualidad del fútbol español, su nueva vida tras la retirada y su etapa en la Roma. El exjugador del Sporting ha sido especialmente contundente al abordar las polémicas arbitrales y las continuas quejas de los grandes clubes. "Yo siempre digo que siempre se quejan los que más se tienen que callar", ha asegurado Cote, que no entiende las protestas de Real Madrid y Barcelona por las decisiones de los colegiados. "Pero cómo os podéis quejar vosotros, Madrid, Barcelona... Quien sea, si sois los más beneficiados", ha señalado el exfutbolista, antes de explicar por qué considera que los equipos más poderosos parten con ventaja en determinadas situaciones. "Al final un árbitro cuando está pitando, si está pitando al Madrid y al Sporting, entiendo que tenga mucho más miedo en tomar una decisión en contra del Real Madrid o del Barcelona", ha reflexionado. Cote ha insistido en su crítica a las protestas arbitrales de los grandes: "Pero no pueden venir diciendo, no, es que siempre nos roban. ¿Cómo? Por favor, joder... No, no, por ahí sí que yo no paso, la verdad, no entiendo las quejas de los equipos grandes. Es quejarse por quejarse". Más allá de la polémica arbitral, Cote también ha analizado el momento futbolístico del Real Madrid de José Mourinho. El exlateral ha reconocido que no termina de convencerle el juego del conjunto blanco. "No tener a Kroos se nota. Yo, como como aficionado, veo al Madrid y no me dice nada, su estilo de fútbol o lo que practica no me llama la atención", ha explicado. Además, considera que al equipo le falta una identidad más definida: "No le veo con balón un rigor como podría ver al City de Guardiola o equipos así, que es lo que a mí me llama la atención". Su comparación con el eterno rival ha sido clara: "Yo, por ejemplo, disfruto mucho más viendo al Barcelona que al Madrid". Eso sí, también ha reconocido una virtud del conjunto blanco: "El Madrid es el único equipo que es capaz de ganar no jugando bien y eso es también de tener en cuenta". Preguntado por Mbappé, Cote ha descartado que el francés sea uno de los grandes problemas del equipo. "Mbappé no creo que sea un problema, creo que es un jugadorazo y tiene el nivel para estar en el Madrid hasta cuando él quiera", ha afirmado. El exjugador también ha mostrado su sorpresa por el regreso de Mourinho al Real Madrid, especialmente después de la apuesta anterior por Xabi Alonso. "Creo que Xabi Alonso era el entrenador ideal para Madrid, pero bueno, como dije antes, desconozco lo que pasaría y tomaron la decisión que como aficionado nunca hubiese tomado", ha asegurado. Sobre Mourinho, al que se enfrentó durante su etapa en el Sporting, Cote ha recordado tanto los momentos de tensión como los buenos gestos del portugués. "Luego también Mourinho vino, nos felicitó a todos y por esa parte también hay que aplaudirle porque no todo el mundo lo hace", ha explicado. También ha dejado una reflexión sobre la personalidad del entrenador: "Muchas veces tu personaje te acaba comiendo la persona, entonces hay que tener mucho cuidado en ese sentido". Cote ha aprovechado su paso por La Tribu para hablar de su nueva etapa tras colgar las botas. Actualmente trabaja como segundo entrenador de la selección asturiana sub-16, aunque todavía está adaptándose a su nuevo papel. "Siempre me llamó la atención los banquillos, sé que a día de hoy no me veo de primer entrenador, pero bueno, me gusta el fútbol, creo que lo entiendo", ha confesado. También ha recordado su paso por la Roma y una curiosa anécdota con Francesco Totti, que apareció después de que Cote sufriera un accidente de tráfico junto a su mujer y Bojan. "Y entonces apareció Francesco, y claro, ahí Totti es Dios, y entonces él cogió y paró el coche ahí en medio de la carretera", ha relatado.
